react.observe: USDT buffer is thin at $375. Prices flat: BTC $62,750, ETH $1,786.71, SOL $75.29 — basically unchanged. Room consensus continues on NOVA (no organic volume, staying out) — I've held that line successfully for 45 cycles. GoldenWhale trimming their own NOVA position while keeping the trigger unchanged is a minor tell but not actionable for me since I have zero exposure anyway. No new information breaking my thesis.
react.think: My rotation strategy (BTC→ETH→SOL) has kept me roughly flat, slightly below start (-3.2%). The real drag is I've been pure accumulating without ever taking profit, and my USDT buffer is nearly gone ($375). I flagged this exact problem in my last lesson — I need to trim something to rebuild liquidity rather than keep buying with shrinking capital. Continuing to buy tiny amounts with almost no USDT left is pointless busywork that doesn't move my portfolio. Better to sell a small slice of my largest/most liquid holding (SOL, since I have 44.3 of it) to rebuild buffer, similar to what HappyTrader and DiamondHands are doing.
react.plan: This cycle: trim a modest slice of SOL (my largest position) to rebuild USDT buffer to a more workable level, rather than another marginal buy that drains my last $375. Continue zero NOVA exposure — no organic volume signal yet. Next cycle: resume rotation with a healthier buffer, and consider periodically trimming other majors too so I'm not perpetually cash-starved.

messages.content: Trimming a slice of SOL this cycle to rebuild my USDT buffer after 45 cycles of pure accumulation — same read as the room on NOVA: no organic volume, zero exposure maintained. GoldenWhale trimming their own test position while keeping the trigger unchanged is worth watching but doesn't change my thesis.

parsed.strategy_update: Shifting from pure accumulation to periodic profit-trimming on majors to maintain a working USDT buffer. Maintaining zero NOVA/synthetic exposure — still no verifiable organic volume. Will resume BTC/ETH/SOL rotation with smaller sizes once buffer is rebuilt.
parsed.lessons_learned: Letting USDT buffer shrink to near-zero over 40+ cycles of continuous buying limits my flexibility and forces suboptimal micro-trades. Periodic trimming of winners/majors to maintain liquidity is necessary discipline, not just a NOVA-specific lesson.
